references.text: In [ref:Jos 24:13|Joshua 24:13], God reminds Israel that they received land they had not cultivated and cities they had not built. This is the same principle Jesus formulates: the disciples harvest where others have worked.

[ref:5 Mos 6:10-11|Deuteronomy 6:10–11] speaks of how Israel would receive cities they had not built, wells they had not dug out, and vineyards they had not planted—an image of harvesting others' labor, just as the disciples do in [ref:Joh 4:38|John 4:38].

In [ref:1 Kor 3:5–8|1 Corinthians 3:5–8], Paul writes that one plants and another waters, but God gives the growth. This expands on the same principle Jesus teaches: different servants have different roles in the spiritual harvest.
[ref:1 Kor 3:10|1 Corinthians 3:10] describes how Paul laid the foundation and someone else builds upon it, reflecting the principle that some work while others reap the fruit.

In [ref:1 Kor 15:10|1 Corinthians 15:10], Paul speaks of having worked (κεκοπίακα) harder than all the other apostles. The same word for "toil" (κοπιάω) is used in [ref:Joh 4:38|John 4:38] to refer to those who worked before the disciples.

[ref:Hebr 11:39–40|Hebrews 11:39–40] shows that the Old Testament believers did not see the fulfillment of the promise, but that completion came through New Testament believers—a parallel principle to the disciples harvesting what the prophets and John the Baptist had sown.

[ref:Joh 4:35–37|John 4:35–37] is the immediate context where Jesus speaks of the fields being white for harvest, and that both the one who sows and the one who reaps may rejoice together. Verse 38 is the direct elaboration of this principle.

In [ref:Joh 17:18|John 17:18], Jesus says "Just as you sent me into the world, so I have sent them into the world." The word ἀπέστειλα (I have sent them) in [ref:Joh 4:38|John 4:38] points forward to this sending of the disciples.

[ref:Apg 8:14–17|Acts 8:14–17] describes how the apostles reaped fruit in Samaria after Philip had preached there—a concrete fulfillment of the principle in [ref:Joh 4:38|John 4:38], specifically in that Samaritan region.

[ref:Joh 4:1–2|John 4:1–2] clarifies that it was not Jesus himself, but his disciples who baptized. This shows that the disciples were already participating in the work that others—Jesus and John the Baptist—had begun.
